title: Show Fuji Film Simulation in LrC
text:
When I imported my first Fuji RAW+JPEG images into Lightroom Classic (LrC) two things became apparent.
Firstly, only the RAW images were displayed by default. I’d taken a number of images with Fuji’s much loved film simulations applied (e.g. Classic Chrome, Reala Ace, Velvia Vivid etc.). However, these simulations are only applied to the JPEG images and hence I was unable to see their effect on the image. Thankfully, this was quickly resolved by selecting a checkbox, ‘Treat JPEG files next to raw files as separate photos’, in Lightroom’s Preferences. Now RAW and JPEG images appeared separately, side-by-side in the Library Module.
Secondly, there was no way to display the film simulation applied to each JPEG or filter images by film simulation.

title: Show Fuji Film Simulation in LrC
text:
Method
After a little investigation it turned out that the film simulation is baked into the JPEG and stored in Fujufilm’s private maker-note tags. However, LrC does not surface that maker-note field. You can see it with ExifTool (exiftool -FilmMode *.jpg), but inside LrC there is no “Film Simulation” column and no way to filter or build Smart Collections by it.

title: Show Fuji Film Simulation in LrC
text:
Result
Were applicable, JPEG images now show the film simulation name above each thumbnail in Grid view. In addition, the images can be grouped and filtered by film simulation.

title: My first photography project
text:
Today I completed my first photography project on the new website!
Unsurprisingly, it’s to do with my new camera, though I didn’t expect to be scripting automations this early, after returning to an old hobby that’s been neglected for a decade … I guess you can’t take the developer out of me 😜
Fuji’s film simulations (sims) garner alot of hype and are often cited as the reason why people buy Fuji cameras. I was keen to try them on my first foray out with the X100vi. Arriving back at my Mac and importing my images into Lightroom Classic (LrC) I was a little disappointed that I couldn’t see the sims applied to each image nor filter my images by the sim used.
With an itch to stratch, the automation project was conceived …
